The issue here is clear. After calling `helper_a(sk, 0)`, the verifier loses track of the packet pointer validity. 

When `bpf_skb_pull_data` is called, it can invalidate packet pointers (the packet data may be reallocated). The verifier knows this - after calling a function that can invalidate packet pointers, all previously validated packet pointers become invalid ("scalar").

The bounds check `if ((void *)(p + 1) > (void *)(long)sk->data_end)` is done BEFORE the `helper_a` call. 

After `helper_a` returns, `p` is still pointing to the old packet data, but the verifier has marked it as invalid since `bpf_skb_pull_data` can change the packet layout. The fix is to reload `p` from `sk->data` and redo the bounds check after the function call.
